title: Single Number II
prompt: Given an integer array `nums` where every element appears exactly three times except for one, which appears exactly once, find and return the single element. You must implement a solution with linear runtime complexity and use only constant extra space.

examples.explanation: With only one element, it is trivially the single number since there are no triples to cancel out.

constraints: Each element appears exactly three times except for one element which appears exactly once
hints: Simple XOR won't work here, since it only cancels pairs — you need something that cancels triples instead.
Think bit by bit: for each of the 32 bit positions, sum up how many numbers have a 1 in that position across the whole array.
If you sum each bit position across all numbers, every bit contributed by a tripled number is a multiple of 3. So (sum of that bit position) mod 3 recovers the corresponding bit of the single number.

solution.approach: For each of the 32 bit positions, count how many numbers in the array have a 1 bit there. Since every number except the answer appears exactly three times, its bits contribute multiples of 3 to each position's count. Taking that count modulo 3 leaves exactly the bit contributed by the single unique number, and reassembling all 32 such bits reconstructs it. Handle the sign bit separately since Python has arbitrary-precision integers rather than fixed 32-bit wraparound.
